transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—please come in and have a seat. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with?

I’ve been really struggling to keep my projects organized at work, and it feels like everything is slipping through the cracks. No matter how many lists, calendars, or apps I try, I still end up feeling overwhelmed and out of control, and it’s starting to affect my job.

Have you had similar problems with focus, organization, or sitting still since you were a child or teenager, or is this difficulty with keeping projects organized something that started only in the last few years?

I think these kinds of issues have been around since I was a kid, just not as obvious. Teachers used to say I daydreamed a lot and had trouble staying in my seat, and my mom would have to keep reminding me to finish chores or homework because I’d wander off halfway through. It’s really in the last couple of years, with this new role and more responsibility, that it’s become a lot more noticeable and disruptive.

Over the past month, have you often felt persistently nervous or on edge, or down and unable to enjoy things, or does it feel more like being chronically stressed and overextended without strong anxiety or sadness?

I’d say it’s mostly feeling chronically stressed and overextended, like I’m constantly behind and can’t catch up. I do get anxious when I think about work or performance reviews, but I wouldn’t describe it as feeling really depressed or unable to enjoy anything.

Outside of work, do you also have long‑standing problems with things like losing items, forgetting appointments, or staying organized at home and in your personal life, or are these issues mainly limited to your current job role?

It definitely shows up outside of work too. I’m always misplacing things like my work badge, AirPods, or papers I just had in my hand, and I have to set multiple reminders for appointments or I’ll forget them. The new job just made those tendencies a lot more obvious and harder to hide.

Thinking back to when you were in elementary or middle school, did these attention and organization problems noticeably affect your grades, behavior reports, or ability to keep up with schoolwork and activities, or were you generally able to function fine despite the tendencies to daydream and be reminded about chores?

I was generally able to function okay and keep my grades up, but it took a lot of effort and reminders from my mom. My report cards would have comments like “bright but easily distracted” or “needs to stay on task,” and I’d often forget parts of assignments or leave things half-finished unless someone checked in on me.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you—please come in and have a seat. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a lifelong pattern, beginning in childhood, of inattention, disorganization, forgetfulness, and difficulty completing tasks that has now become more impairing with increased job demands. Symptoms are present across settings (school, home, work) and have led to functional impairment at work and in daily life. There is no indication of a primary mood or anxiety disorder driving the difficulties; rather, chronic stress appears secondary to the attentional and organizational problems. This pattern is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive type (F90.0). Z73.0 (burn-out) was considered but does not explain the longstanding, cross-situational symptoms starting in childhood.
